### Usage

List the selected host’s project hierarchy.

### Inputs

Optional host selects the daemon.

### Invariants

The result describes registered hierarchy, not every discoverable directory.

### Effects

Returns a hierarchy snapshot without changing registrations.

### Recovery

Refresh after mutations or host reconnection.

post.description:
### Usage

Apply a hierarchy action on a host.

### Inputs

Send host and an input object with an action and its action-specific fields; JSON is limited to 384 KiB.

### Invariants

Registration and discovery are distinct; the host validates action preconditions. listProjectIcons scans at most five directory levels and 2,000 entries, returning at most 24 icons of at most 256 KiB. It skips hidden names, symlinks, node_modules, vendor, dist and release, and applies Git ignore rules when available. Results are best-effort.

### Effects

Actions can change project or workspace registration and presentation.

### Recovery

After an uncertain mutation, fetch the hierarchy before deciding whether to repeat it.

input.description: Action-specific hierarchy query or mutation; ids and host paths select registrations, while nullable project metadata clears values.

anyOf.description: Base64 image data URL, including SVG, up to 256 KiB decoded; null clears the project icon.
Workspace-level omp launch configuration; only affects omp children spawned for that workspace.

advisor.description: Whether to launch with advisor mode.

extraArgs.description: Extra OMP CLI args, stored as an array.

delete.description:
### Usage

Revoke a linked host by id.

### Inputs

The id query parameter identifies the remote host; local cannot be revoked.

### Invariants

A cluster member leaves before its host record is revoked; an unreadable host registry prevents pool changes.

### Effects

Removes the record, closes its link, aborts broker requests and notifies listeners; future daemon reconnects are unauthorized.

### Recovery

Supply a known remote id or repair registry storage before retrying.

patch.description:
### Usage

Update host settings or rename one pool without replacing the registry.

### Inputs

JSON host id and at least one of label, allowAgentStart or shareCredentials; alternatively poolId and label.

### Invariants

The local host cannot change agent-start or credential-sharing settings; an empty local label resets its name.

### Effects

Persists changes and notifies listeners; disabling effective credential sharing aborts broker requests.

### Recovery

Correct invalid input, use an existing host or pool, or repair unavailable registry storage.

### Usage

Create a linked host and obtain its one-time enrollment token.

### Inputs

JSON label, trimmed and non-empty, at most 100 characters.

### Invariants

The token is returned at creation, not in subsequent host snapshots; the login command uses the request's externally visible origin.

### Effects

Persists the host and notifies listeners.

### Recovery

Correct an invalid label or repair the host registry before retrying.

### Usage

Replace the complete pool registry.

### Inputs

JSON object with a pools array of pool, member and project configurations.

### Invariants

Members must reference known hosts; pool configurations are validated before persistence.

### Effects

Saves pools, notifies listeners and aborts broker requests for hosts that lose credential sharing.

### Recovery

Correct invalid configurations on 400; repair unreadable or unwritable registries on 503.

delete.description:
### Usage

Remove a host from the cluster and restore its prior daemon configuration.

### Inputs

Host id path parameter; no JSON body is required.

### Invariants

Pool removal is persisted before restoration; restoration failure does not undo the leave.

### Effects

Saves pools, notifies listeners, aborts broker requests unless independently shared, and attempts daemon configuration restore.

### Recovery

Inspect optional restoreError in a successful response; synchronization can retry a missed restore. Repair pool storage on 503.

put.description:
### Usage

Join a linked remote host to this server's cluster.

### Inputs

Host id path parameter and JSON object containing only an absolute projectsRoot.

### Invariants

Joining hosts must be ready and cannot hold another server's cluster configuration; the local master is added automatically when needed.

### Effects

Gathers project facts, saves the cluster, notifies listeners and attempts to apply the master configuration to the joined daemon; an apply failure does not undo the join.

### Recovery

Resolve readiness or ownership conflicts, retry a concurrent cluster change, or repair pool storage; daemon synchronization can apply a missed configuration later.

delete.description:
### Usage

Delete an allowed auth-broker credential block through the sharing proxy.

### Inputs

Supply host bearer authentication and an allowed path; query and selected headers pass through, and a body is limited to 1 MiB.

### Invariants

Admission is repeated after reading the body; disallowed paths are refused and payload semantics belong to the broker.

### Effects

Forwards the deletion and passes through upstream status and body; revocation can abort in-flight work.

### Recovery

After an uncertain response, consult broker state before repeating the deletion.

### Additional protocol details

Only content-type, accept, if-none-match, and omp-auth-broker-capabilities request headers and content-type, etag, cache-control, and vary response headers pass through. Query strings are forwarded; broker payload formats are intentionally opaque.

parameters.name: id

413.description: Request body exceeds 1 MiB.

502.description: The broker request failed or was aborted.

Read an allowed auth-broker resource through the host credential-sharing proxy.

### Inputs

### Additional protocol details

get.description:
### Usage

Download a file belonging to the current cluster configuration.

### Inputs

Authenticate as a cluster member and supply the lowercase 64-character content hash in the path.

### Invariants

Membership is checked again after building the configuration; hashes absent from the current manifest, including older versions, return 404.

### Effects

Returns raw application/octet-stream bytes with no-store; it does not apply configuration.

### Recovery

Fetch a fresh manifest if the hash is no longer present; restore membership or service availability after an admission failure.

### Additional protocol details

The hash addresses content in the current manifest, not an older configuration.

Fetch the master's current mirrored configuration manifest.

### Usage

Connect a host daemon's WebSocket to the server hub.

### Inputs

Supply the host bearer token and WebSocket upgrade request.

### Invariants

The hub authenticates before upgrading; the ordinary proxy gate does not handle this path.

### Effects

A successful upgrade hands the socket to the hub rather than returning a normal HTTP response.

### Recovery

Reconnect after a dropped link; an upgrade refusal requires correcting authentication or availability.

### Additional protocol details

The hello is the first WebSocket frame. The server refuses upgrades while shutting down.

The hello body is inspected for its version, but malformed or oversized bodies are also refused.

get.description:
### Usage

Retrieve the installable web app manifest, subject to the configured web-password guard.

### Inputs

The optional theme query supplies a theme color; invalid or absent values use black. Request headers determine the install name.

### Invariants

Packaged icon bytes are read and encoded once when the server module loads; the name and color are resolved per request. The response is private and must be revalidated.

### Effects

Reads a snapshot; embedded data URLs let installers load icons without separate authenticated requests.

### Recovery

Retry after authentication if required; changed packaged icons require a server module reload.

get.description:
### Usage

Inspect local user/project MCP configuration and optionally a session's live inventory.

### Inputs

cwd is optional and must be allowed; live=0 disables live lookup, attach=1 avoids starting a session, and advisor=1 applies only to a fresh spawn.

### Invariants

Without cwd there is no project config. User secrets are not returned and project server configuration is redacted; live errors are sanitized.

### Effects

Reads local files; a live lookup with sessionId may start a local session unless attach=1.

### Recovery

Inspect liveError separately from configuration; use attach=1 to avoid spawning while retrying.

### Additional protocol details

Project server env and headers are redacted; user servers expose only status and type. Live errors are sanitized.

Enable, disable or reload MCP servers in a selected local session.

Provide sessionId and action; enable and disable also require a validated server name.

May start the selected local session and sends a native MCP command to it.

### Recovery

Wait for a busy turn to finish; after an uncertain response inspect live inventory before repeating.

get.description:
### Usage

Fetch a content-addressed tool-result image or thumbnail.

### Inputs

hash is a SHA-256 content identifier; presence of thumb requests a preview.

### Invariants

Remote bytes must match the hash; non-images return 415 and missing images return 404.

### Effects

May fetch from linked hosts and cache a local copy or thumbnail; full images are privately immutable-cached.

### Recovery

If thumbnail generation fails the full image is served without immutable caching, allowing a later preview.

### Additional protocol details

thumb is presence-based and requests a WebP thumbnail; if thumbnail generation fails the original image is returned. Hash is SHA-256.

get.description:
### Usage

Read the global model selector snapshot and current Anthropic slow-mode setting.

### Inputs

The legacy cwd query does not affect the result.

### Invariants

Model data is cached globally for 60 seconds; models.yml changes invalidate the cache and restart the utility process. Slow mode is read separately on every request. The HTTP response adds anthropicSlowMode, and each modelList entry includes thinkingLevels plus contextWindow and maxTokens when supplied by omp, in tokens.

### Effects

Queries omp on cache misses; failures return a safe empty snapshot with an error marker.

### Recovery

Inspect the error marker and configuration before retrying.

### Usage

Refresh the global model selector snapshot from configured providers.

### Inputs

No request body is required; the legacy cwd query does not affect the result.

### Invariants

Bypasses both the web cache and omp discovery cache; successful responses have the same shape as GET. Concurrent GET requests join the refresh. Active sessions are not stopped.

### Effects

Runs online discovery, refreshes command-backed credentials, and replaces the cached snapshot on success.

### Recovery

A 503 indicates discovery or loading failed; inspect provider configuration and retry.

### Usage

Search models.dev and obtain a model preset recommendation.

### Inputs

q and provider are truncated to 120 characters, baseUrl to 500; limit defaults to 50.

### Invariants

Provider and base URL are ranking and recommendation hints, not credentials. Catalog entries cache for one hour and stale entries survive fetch failure.

### Effects

May fetch the remote catalog; does not write model configuration.

### Recovery

If no cached catalog exists and the fetch fails, retry after the upstream service recovers.

post.description:
### Usage

Check that an isolated omp registry resolves a candidate model.

### Inputs

Provide providerName, provider object and model object with an ID; latencyMs is milliseconds.

### Invariants

This is configuration discovery, not a completion or credential connectivity test; the isolated agent directory excludes stored credentials.

### Effects

Starts an isolated utility process and writes then removes a temporary models.yml; it does not save the candidate to user configuration.

### Recovery

Inspect validation or resolution errors before retrying; a successful resolution does not prove credentials work.

### Additional protocol details

Runs isolated registry discovery only; no completion or credential contact.

Returns publicKey and subscribed; obtaining the key can generate and persist VAPID keys.

### Recovery

If unsubscribed, register a browser push subscription and save it with PUT.

put.description:
### Usage

Synchronize this device's notification preferences and optionally its push subscription.

### Inputs

JSON deviceId (8–64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens), prefs and optional subscription with HTTPS endpoint and push keys.

### Invariants

Omitted subscription preserves the stored one; invalid or missing preference fields use defaults, rather than preserving previous preferences. A push endpoint belongs to one device.

### Effects

Persists the device, may evict another device with the same endpoint, and returns subscribed.

### Recovery

On 400 invalid_device or invalid_subscription, correct the submitted device ID or subscription and retry.

prefs.description: Per-device notification preferences; unrecognized or invalid fields are normalized to defaults when saved.

enabled.description: Whether this device requests notifications; defaults to false.

completed.description: Notify when a session completes; defaults to true.

error.description: Notify on errors; defaults to true.

input.description: Notify when input is requested; defaults to true.

modelSwitch.description: Notify on model switches; defaults to false.

whenActive.description: Delivery preference while a reachable tab is active; defaults to toast.

### Usage

Remove one history entry by id or explicitly clear all history.

### Inputs

Query id is a nonempty string up to 256 characters; alternatively use all=1 with no id. No body is read.

### Invariants

A valid id takes precedence over all; an invalid present id never clears history. Unknown IDs are harmless.

### Effects

Deletes the selected entry or all entries and returns ok.

### Recovery

On 400 invalid_history_request, supply a valid id or omit id and explicitly set all=1.

get.description:
### Usage

Load the persistent notification center history.

### Inputs

No parameters.

### Invariants

Entries are newest first, limited to the latest 100; events requested by at least one enabled device are recorded even if undelivered.

### Effects

Returns entries without marking them read.

### Recovery

Reload history to reconcile the client mirror after a failed mutation.

patch.description:
### Usage

Mark only entries the client has shown as read.

### Inputs

JSON ids array of at most 100 nonempty strings, each at most 256 characters; body limit 32 KiB.

### Invariants

Unknown IDs and an empty array are harmless; replacing a session/type entry later creates a new notification with its own read state.

### Effects

Marks matching stored entries read and returns ok.

### Recovery

Correct malformed requests after 400 invalid_history_request or reduce the body after 413 request_too_large.

post.description:
### Usage

Report tab activity and the conversation currently on screen; refresh while present and on visibility or session changes.

### Inputs

JSON clientId and deviceId (8–64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens), boolean visible, safe-integer seq, and optional sessionId.

### Invariants

Empty or non-string sessionId becomes null. Sequence numbers order reports per client: strictly older reports are ignored, while equal numbers replace the report. Presence expires after 60 seconds.

### Effects

Updates in-memory routing presence and returns 204, including for an ignored older report.

### Recovery

On 400 invalid_presence correct the report; send a newer sequence on subsequent updates or refreshes.

post.description:
### Usage

Send a test push to the specified device and report whether the push service accepted it.

### Inputs

JSON deviceId of 8–64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens.

### Invariants

This is one push attempt, not a delivery receipt; test events do not enter normal notification history.

### Effects

Sends a test push and returns 204 on acceptance; a rejected subscription may be removed.

### Recovery

Correct a 400 invalid_device; for 502 push_failed, inspect the error and restore the device subscription or push service before retrying.

put.description:
### Usage

Update native user settings.

### Inputs

Provide a settings object; enabledModels is checked for ambiguous bare IDs when a catalog is available.

### Invariants

The writer preserves unrelated configuration keys; unavailable omp does not prevent editing.

### Effects

Writes configuration and invalidates model cache and utility process when model-selection settings change.

### Recovery

Read settings after an uncertain response before retrying.

### Additional protocol details

Writes the supported settings allowlist, preserving unrelated configuration.

post.description:
### Usage

Restart running omp RPC sessions after the runner shipped with keylime changes; this endpoint does not install the runner.

### Inputs

Send application/json containing exactly {action:"restart"}, at most 4096 bytes.

### Invariants

Browser-origin requests must pass the origin check. The returned count is the number reported restarted, not an update installation status.

### Effects

Restarts running RPC sessions and can disrupt their connections.

### Recovery

A failed or interrupted request may have restarted some sessions; inspect session state before retrying, since another request can restart them again.

### Usage

Inspect the installed omp runner version, which may differ from the web build version.

### Inputs

No parameters.

### Invariants

The result may be null when the binary is missing or its probe fails; successful probes are cached with file-fingerprint invalidation and expiry, and misses have a short backoff.

### Effects

May probe the installed executable; does not change it.

### Recovery

Retry after the probe backoff if the binary was installed or repaired; a cached result may persist until invalidated or expired.

post.description:
### Usage

Read or edit Repo and System notebooks and task boards, improve the contents of a task's Brief editor, or launch a saved task.

### Inputs

Select an owning daemon and stable Repo or System ID. Writes use the current revision. Notes and tasks accept PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP attachments. If launch or resume returns a review, repeat that action with confirmation and selected refs. Maximum request size is 8 MiB.

### Invariants

Improvement sends the Brief, target name and selected task images, never shared Notes or checkout contents. Saved attachment IDs must belong to the task.

### Effects

Improvement returns replacement text without saving edits. Launch snapshots saved Notes and task images (at most ten images and 5 MiB combined) with the literal first message. Refresh never resends an uncertain message.

### Recovery

Read the board after a conflict or lost reply. Resume a stale, unadmitted Effort to review a fresh plan under the same launch ID. Admitted Efforts retry their saved setup; never resend if first-message delivery is uncertain.

### Usage

Install, remove, update, enable or disable plugins through omp.

### Inputs

### Invariants

Without cwd only global changes are available; update without source upgrades all.

### Effects

Executes the local omp CLI, potentially downloading packages and changing files and configuration.

### Recovery

Inspect plugin inventory after timeout or disconnect before repeating a mutation.

get.description:
### Usage

List managed projects across hosts.

### Inputs

This request has no path input; each project retains its owning host.

### Invariants

The list aggregates registered projects rather than browsing every directory.

### Effects

Returns a snapshot assembled from host state.

### Recovery

Refresh when hosts reconnect or registrations change.

### Usage

Update registered project presentation.

### Inputs

Send hostId and a project update or updates array of at most 500 entries.

### Invariants

Each cwd must match a registered project; poolId is rejected.

### Effects

Updates are applied sequentially, so earlier changes may survive a later error.

### Recovery

Fetch the project list after an error or disconnect before retrying.

post.description:
### Usage

Clone a project and stream progress frames.

### Inputs

Send an id, destination parent, repository URL and optional hostId; paths are on that host.

### Invariants

The client-provided id identifies the host clone job; progress is read with an advancing cursor.

### Effects

Starts a host clone; request abort or stream cancellation asks the host to cancel.

### Recovery

Disconnect cancellation is best effort and may race completion; inspect the destination before retrying.

### Additional protocol details

Streams newline-delimited JSON frames until done, cancelled or error. A reset output frame clears previous progress; disconnect cancels the clone. clone_uncertain means inspect the destination before retrying.

### Usage

Read provider usage for an optional provider and model context.

### Inputs

Identifiers are trimmed, 1–200 characters from letters, digits, dot, underscore, colon, slash and hyphen; refresh=true requests refresh.

### Invariants

Invalid supplied identifiers return 400; omitted identifiers are not filters.

### Effects

May query upstream usage and use cached usage data; no provider configuration is changed.

### Recovery

Retry a 502 when usage becomes available, optionally requesting refresh.

get.description:
### Usage

Poll the cross-host session inventory together with currently running registered wrappers.

### Inputs

Optional id filters only sessions, not runningSessionIds or runningSessions; an unfiltered request may supply If-None-Match.

### Invariants

Host inventories can be cached internally; running wrappers are sampled at request time. Unfiltered responses have an ETag and may return 304; filtered responses do not.

### Effects

Read-only inventory and live-wrapper lookup; responses prohibit browser and proxy storage.

### Recovery

Re-poll for changes and retain the previous unfiltered body on 304; a partial host inventory is not proof a session is absent everywhere.

delete.description:
### Usage

Permanently remove an active session from its owning host.

### Inputs

id identifies the session; no body is used.

### Invariants

The host must be online; the live child is stopped and flushed before deletion. Live children are excluded from on-disk reparenting because their processes own their files.

### Effects

Deletes the session, updates eligible child references, clears exited state and invalidates the host list; unpinned replacement metadata is cleaned up best-effort.

### Recovery

A lost response may follow deletion; inspect the owning host before retrying. Offline or failed discovery is not evidence of deletion.

x-client-semantics.Effects: Deletes the session, updates eligible child references, clears exited state and invalidates the host list; unpinned replacement metadata is cleaned up best-effort.
x-client-semantics.Inputs: id identifies the session; no body is used.
x-client-semantics.Invariants: The host must be online; the live child is stopped and flushed before deletion. Live children are excluded from on-disk reparenting because their processes own their files.
x-client-semantics.Recovery: A lost response may follow deletion; inspect the owning host before retrying. Offline or failed discovery is not evidence of deletion.
x-client-semantics.Usage: Permanently remove an active session from its owning host.

get.description:
### Usage

Read a session's persisted transcript from its owning host, optionally with live agent state.

### Inputs

id selects the session; deferThinking and deferMedia defer payloads; includeState requests live wrapper state. tail selects the newest 1–200 display entries, and before plus historyRevision selects an exclusive preceding page.

### Invariants

Tail pages are chronological on the active branch, without overlap. Continuations omit session metadata and navigation tree. historyRevision identifies the file generation; a stale revision or missing active cursor returns 409 session_history_changed. Without tail the full transcript is returned. agent is omitted if its live state request fails. Disk and live state are not an atomic snapshot.

### Effects

Reads host session storage and may send get_state to an existing wrapper; it does not start a process.

### Recovery

On session_history_changed discard partial pages and synchronize again. Fetch agent state separately when omitted; retry reads when the host is available.

parameters.description: Include live agent state if available.
parameters.name: includeState

parameters.description: Return at most this many newest active-branch display entries (1–200).
parameters.name: tail

parameters.description: Exclusive oldest entry ID from a preceding tail response; requires tail and historyRevision.
parameters.name: before

parameters.description: Opaque revision from the first page; required with before.
parameters.name: historyRevision

patch.description:
### Usage

Set a session title on its owning process or persisted file.

### Inputs

JSON name must be nonblank; surrounding whitespace is removed. The request is limited to 64 KiB.

### Invariants

A live process owns its file; a busy history edit fences fallback file writes. A new live session can be renamed before its file exists.

### Effects

Sends set_session_name to the live process or updates the host file and invalidates session lists.

### Recovery

Wait for a busy edit to finish; after a lost response read the current title before deciding whether to retry.

post.description:
### Usage

Move a session and its sibling artifacts into its host's native archive.

### Inputs

id selects the active session; no body is used.

### Invariants

Archive child sessions first: a parent with active children is rejected. The host must be online and a live child must flush before the move.

### Effects

Stops the session process as needed, archives its files, clears exited state and invalidates the host inventory.

### Recovery

After an uncertain response inspect both active and archive inventories on the owning host; an unavailable host's omission is not proof of absence.

### Additional protocol details

Stops the live child and archives the session and artifacts; children must be archived first.

### Usage

Generate a session title or fall back to an existing or first-message-derived title.

### Inputs

id selects the session; no request body is used.

### Invariants

generated distinguishes native generation from fallback; usage is null. No user message and no existing title yields a conflict; a history edit fences fallback writes.

### Effects

May start an RPC process and invoke native title generation; a derived fallback is persisted and synced to a live process best-effort.

### Recovery

Wait for a busy session; after an uncertain response read its current title before requesting another generation.

post.description:
### Usage

Send an ordered batch of navigation or input actions to a session-owned browser tab.

### Inputs

id identifies the session; the body supplies the exact tab and 1–64 actions in order, within 1 MiB of UTF-8 JSON.

### Invariants

The whole batch is validated before effects; the runner rechecks ownership before each action without starting a runner or exposing CDP.

### Effects

Applies actions sequentially; other viewers and the agent remain able to interact. Failure stops the batch and may leave an applied prefix.

### Recovery

Never automatically retry a failed batch or its remaining actions: partial delivery may be uncertain.

### Additional protocol details

Applies 1–64 navigation or input actions in array order to a session-owned tab; request bodies are capped at 1 MiB. The whole batch is validated before dispatch. A failed request may have applied a prefix; never automatically retry it or the remaining actions.

### Usage

Capture a read-only JPEG frame of a session-owned browser tab.

### Inputs

id identifies the live session and tabId identifies a tab returned by discovery.

### Invariants

The host and runner recheck ownership; callers cannot supply a CDP endpoint or browser input.

### Effects

Captures one frame and reports its CSS viewport dimensions in response headers without managing a browser.

### Recovery

Rediscover tabs after session or tab changes, or retry when the host reconnects.

### Additional protocol details

Captures one JPEG from a tab owned by the live session. X-Browser-Viewport-Width and X-Browser-Viewport-Height report CSS viewport dimensions. This read-only request does not change browser lifecycle.

get.description:
### Usage

Read the selected transcript context, synchronize display history, or obtain the current persisted boundary.

### Inputs

leafId selects a branch; presence of deferThinking, deferMedia or includePreCompaction enables each option. sync=1 accepts an opaque cursor and a positive limit up to 200; boundary=1 excludes sync, leafId, includePreCompaction, cursor and limit.

### Invariants

Sync pages append or replace when a branch or compaction invalidates the cursor; use the returned cursor in the same session and view. Live output is sampled after the disk read only for the current tip, so it is not an atomic disk snapshot. Boundary returns current active entry IDs only.

### Effects

Reads persisted history and samples an existing live wrapper; it never spawns one. Sync and boundary responses are no-store. A live session without a file can return an empty initial boundary or sync history.

### Recovery

Honor replace and hasMore when applying pages; do not discard confirmed history merely because a file is temporarily missing. Restart synchronization when the cursor is invalidated.

### Additional protocol details

boundary=1 returns active entry IDs and cannot be combined with sync, leafId, includePreCompaction, cursor or limit. sync=1 returns a history page and optional live snapshot. Deferred flags are enabled by presence.

get.summary: Read session context or synchronized history

x-client-semantics.Effects: Reads persisted history and samples an existing live wrapper; it never spawns one. Sync and boundary responses are no-store. A live session without a file can return an empty initial boundary or sync history.
x-client-semantics.Inputs: leafId selects a branch; presence of deferThinking, deferMedia or includePreCompaction enables each option. sync=1 accepts an opaque cursor and a positive limit up to 200; boundary=1 excludes sync, leafId, includePreCompaction, cursor and limit.
x-client-semantics.Invariants: Sync pages append or replace when a branch or compaction invalidates the cursor; use the returned cursor in the same session and view. Live output is sampled after the disk read only for the current tip, so it is not an atomic disk snapshot. Boundary returns current active entry IDs only.
x-client-semantics.Recovery: Honor replace and hasMore when applying pages; do not discard confirmed history merely because a file is temporarily missing. Restart synchronization when the cursor is invalidated.
x-client-semantics.Usage: Read the selected transcript context, synchronize display history, or obtain the current persisted boundary.

get.description:
### Usage

Fetch a deferred thinking block from persisted session history.

### Inputs

id and entryId identify the session and entry; blockIndex is a required nonnegative safe integer identifying its content block.

### Invariants

The owning host reads the requested block; this is not a live stream or an independent session authorization.

### Effects

Reads stored content without starting an agent process.

### Recovery

If the entry or block is no longer available, refresh the selected history before requesting it again.

get.description:
### Usage

Render persisted session history as self-contained HTML using omp on the owning host.

### Inputs

id identifies the session; inline=1 requests inline disposition only for the local host.

### Invariants

Remote host HTML is always an attachment, even when inline was requested. The result reflects the host's export at request time.

### Effects

Runs the host export operation and returns HTML; it does not mutate the session.

### Recovery

Retry the read when the host and its omp binary are available; restart an interrupted download.

### Additional protocol details

inline=1 is honored only for the local host; remote HTML is always downloaded.

get.description:
### Usage

Resolve a session-local URI to an existing path on the owning host for the file viewer.

### Inputs

uri must have valid local:// syntax; id can be a live alias which is followed to its owning session.

### Invariants

The host applies its own confinement and filename rules and stats the file without reading it. The returned sessionId is the owner, not necessarily the requested alias.

### Effects

Reads host filesystem metadata; no file contents are returned and no agent process is started.

### Recovery

Use the returned owner when opening the file, since a temporary alias can disappear; resolve again if the file moves or the host reconnects.

get.description:
### Usage

Find the best-ranked matches in the active conversation of one session.

### Inputs

q defaults to empty and is limited to 500 characters; limit is a positive bounded decimal and defaults to the search page size.

### Invariants

Every request rereads and reranks the active context; results are a best-first prefix, not an offset page, and may change as the session changes. Matches include submitted skill prompts, not expanded instructions. Pre-compaction entries are excluded.

### Effects

Reads host history with thinking and media deferred; no-store response and no agent spawn.

### Recovery

To load more request a larger prefix and replace the old results rather than concatenating offset pages; refresh after history changes.

### Additional protocol details

Returns the best prefix, not an offset page; results may be reranked as the session changes.

get.description:
### Usage

Reconcile live, exited or host session state together with the web outbox snapshot.

### Inputs

id identifies the session; no query or body is used.

### Invariants

Outbox entries, scope and settlement identifiers accompany every response, including errors and offline hosts. A live wrapper is queried first, then exited state or host state; these are not one atomic snapshot.

### Effects

Reads outbox state and may send get_state to a running wrapper; it does not start an agent.

### Recovery

Treat queued acceptance and settled IDs according to their reported status, not as proof of delivery; reconcile uncertain message IDs before resending and refresh after reconnect.

### Additional protocol details

All responses, including offline errors, carry the outbox snapshot and settlement IDs.

at.description: Exit time in Unix epoch milliseconds.

hostId.description: Absent on this machine, as on `SessionInfo`.

nativeSettledIds.description: Client message IDs reported settled by native processing, when available.

outbox.description: Held messages in the web outbox; acceptance does not itself establish delivery to omp.

items.description: A server-owned message intent retained until native admission or explicit resolution. Web acceptance does not itself mean omp admitted the input; uncertain handoffs are not automatically resent.

advisor.description: Captured at the original send; an explicit retry must not use current preferences.

createdAt.description: Time the web outbox accepted the intent, in Unix epoch milliseconds.

id.description: Client intent ID used to correlate this submission through handoff.

mayHaveBeenSent.description: A lost reply: omp may have it; never resent by itself.

previousEntryIds.description: Only while delivering: authoritative persisted history captured before dispatch, never retained in tombstones.

sessionId.description: Target session owning the delivery queue.

settlement.description: Delivered native input still needs its correlated view; none is an explicit non-message completion.

uploads.description: Upload identifiers associated with this intent, not filesystem paths.

### Usage

Recover the on-disk subagent roster from the parent session's task results.

### Inputs

id identifies the parent session; no body or query is used.

### Invariants

This is persisted history, not a live process roster. A live new session whose file has not appeared returns an empty roster.

### Effects

Reads the owning host's session artifacts without starting a process; persisted results survive page reloads.

### Recovery

Refresh after task results are committed; an empty roster before the session file lands does not prove no task is running.

get.description:
### Usage

Read a subagent transcript page or its final completion artifact from the parent host.

### Inputs

id and a valid subagentId identify the artifacts; fromByte is a numeric byte offset defaulting to zero. mode=completion selects final output; other values select transcript paging.

### Invariants

Completion reads the separate final markdown without loading the transcript and can work when the transcript exceeds its read cap; paging is not a completion signal.

### Effects

Reads persisted sibling artifacts; no agent process is started.

### Recovery

Continue pages using the returned byte position; request completion separately when available, and refresh if an active subagent has not yet written its final artifact.

get.description:
### Usage

Discover archives across the local and registered linked hosts.

### Inputs

No request body or query is used.

### Invariants

Results are sorted newest archivedAt first and tagged with hostId; unavailableHosts identifies hosts whose archives could not be listed. Pending restores remain discovery evidence, not restore targets.

### Effects

Reads archive inventories without starting sessions; the response is no-store.

### Recovery

An absent archive on an unavailable host is not proven absent; reconnect or repair that host and list again before acting on absence.

post.description:
### Usage

Restore a discovered archive to its original owning host.

### Inputs

JSON key identifies an archive on hostId; omitted hostId selects the local host, while blank or null host IDs are invalid.

### Invariants

Pending archives cannot be restored. A serialized session claim requires fresh active-session inventories from every registered host and rejects any active duplicate. Remote restores reserve a daemon-specific token; an uncertain claim remains held until that same daemon fences it and confirms it stopped.

### Effects

Restores the native session and artifacts, invalidates session lists and pumps held outbox messages. A remote restore can continue after a lost connection or server restart.

### Recovery

Do not assume a timeout or replacement daemon proves failure: inspect the owning restore and resolve archive_restore_unconfirmed before retrying. If the original daemon cannot be fenced, operator recovery is required; unavailable hosts prevent the conflict check.

### Additional protocol details

Checks every host for conflicting active sessions. An unconfirmed restore may still be running and remains blocked until its owning host confirms it stopped; restorePending archives are discovery evidence, not restore targets.

post.description:
### Usage

Import a native omp JSONL session into local storage under its authorized workspace.

### Inputs

JSON fileName must be a basename and content must be nonempty JSONL with a session header containing cwd; decoded content is limited to 10 MiB and the encoded request has a separate bound.

### Invariants

The header cwd must already be an authorized existing path. Session header IDs are replaced with a fresh UUID and imported bash fullOutputPath references are stripped; the provided fileName is not the destination path.

### Effects

Writes a new local session file and invalidates local list and file caches; it does not start an agent.

### Recovery

A lost response may still have created a new session; inspect local sessions before retrying, since another import creates another ID and file.

### Additional protocol details

The header cwd must be authorized; the imported session receives a new ID. Decoded content is limited to 10 MiB.

get.description:
### Usage

Stream session content search scores as newline-delimited JSON batches.

### Inputs

q defaults to empty and is limited to 500 characters; each line contains a scores object keyed by session ID.

### Invariants

The allowed session IDs are captured from the cross-host list before scanning; even empty batches are emitted. Local transcript scoring includes submitted skill prompts, not expanded instructions. This is a pull-driven scan, not a resumable cursor or an atomic snapshot.

### Effects

Scans session content as the client reads; response is no-store and proxy buffering is disabled.

### Recovery

Closing the stream stops after the current batch; restart the search from the beginning after disconnect and replace accumulated results as appropriate.

### Additional protocol details

Pull-driven NDJSON; each line is a batch of session ID to score mappings, including empty batches. Cancellation stops the scan.

post.description:
### Usage

Start a ship job.

### Inputs

Send host and the ship input object. In PR modes, optionally send monitorSessionId for a chat in the same workspace.

### Invariants

Monitoring requires host shipMonitorStatus support. The server issues the monitor grant; the host validates ship preconditions and chat ownership. Job acceptance does not mean shipping is complete or monitoring has started.

### Effects

Starts a host job that may mutate Git and remote state. Opted-in monitoring sends feedback links to chat without gating merges.

### Recovery

Poll job status and inspect repository state after an uncertain response before starting another job.

### Additional protocol details

PR modes may opt into feedback links with monitorSessionId for a chat in the same workspace. The host must support shipMonitorStatus. The server issues the grant and checks that the same watch is still active before accepting feedback. Job acceptance does not mean monitoring has started, and monitoring does not gate merges.

### Usage

Stop PR feedback monitoring for a workspace.

### Inputs

Send host, projectPath, path and the monitorId from the workspace PR state.

### Invariants

Only the initiating server link can stop the monitor; a stale id cannot stop a replacement.

### Effects

Revokes the scoped server grant before attempting to stop the daemon watch, even if the host is offline. Does not change the PR or its merge settings.

### Recovery

Refresh workspace state before retrying after an uncertain response.

### Additional protocol details

Revokes the scoped server grant before attempting to stop the daemon watch. An offline or rejected host stop does not restore the grant.

post.description:
### Usage

Upload recording once and follow the returned jobId via GET and claim via DELETE.

### Inputs

Multipart file is required and nonempty, at most 25MB; optional scope is at most 1024 characters, owner is truncated to 128, and after selects send, steer or followup.

### Invariants

Owner identifies the recording tab, not the per-composer claim token; absent after means insert. Jobs and audio live in process memory.

### Effects

Starts one upstream transcription and retains audio for playback or retry; success returns 202.

### Recovery

Missing configuration returns 501, invalid input 400, oversized audio 413 and capacity exhaustion 429. A repeated upload creates a new job, not a deduplicated retry.

delete.description:
### Usage

Claim a done transcript or omit claim to discard the job.

### Inputs

Path jobId and optional query claim (per composer instance) and owner (tab identity), each truncated to 128 characters.

### Invariants

Only the first claim token receives text; the same token can replay its result. Owner has a 15-second first-claim grace and alone receives after; duplicated tabs may share owner but must use distinct claim tokens.

### Effects

A successful claim or discard frees audio, aborts any attempt and leaves a gone tombstone; a claim on unfinished work changes nothing.

### Recovery

Repeat a lost claim response with the same claim token; done without text during owner grace means retry, while other claimants see gone. Missing or expired jobs return 404; tombstones last up to ten minutes and may be pruned.

### Additional protocol details

Without claim, discard. The first claim token may recover the transcript; only its owner receives after.

Poll a transcription job until done, error or gone before claiming it.

Path jobId identifies the process-local job.

Reads job status without claiming or starting work.

Unknown or expired jobs return 404; settled jobs expire after one hour and tombstones after ten minutes or earlier pruning; restart loses the store.

### Additional protocol details

The transcript is only returned by a claim.

### Usage

Retry a failed transcription using its retained audio rather than uploading another job.

### Inputs

Path jobId and optional query owner, truncated to 128 characters, identify the job and retrying tab.

### Invariants

Only an error job with audio starts a new attempt; pending or settled jobs return their current view, preventing duplicate attempts.

### Effects

Reassigns ownership to the retrying tab and launches an upstream request when eligible.

### Recovery

Returns 501 if unconfigured, 429 if pending capacity is full and 404 if missing or expired; retry a busy request later.

post.description:
### Usage

Preview, create, update, or clean up Systems and Efforts, or control a saved service.

### Inputs

Send optional host and action-specific input as JSON, at most 384 KiB. Creation and cleanup require preview confirmation.

### Invariants

An Effort keeps its captured definitions and paths. Service controls select a saved service by ID; they do not take a command or environment override.

### Effects

Actions may persist definitions, admit setup jobs, start or stop service PTYs, or clean up registered worktrees. Service output uses the existing terminal channel.

### Recovery

List host state after uncertain delivery rather than repeating mutations. Retry setup explicitly and refresh the cleanup preview before resuming removal.

get.description:
### Usage

Attach an authenticated client to an existing session terminal.

### Inputs

hostId and sessionId identify the owning host and live session; the first frame is a version 1 hello.

### Invariants

Input belongs only to this socket and is never replayed. Reconnection starts with a fresh snapshot.

### Effects

Input and resize frames are forwarded to the host-owned PTY; detach closes only the attachment.

### Recovery

A disconnected or slow client reconnects and receives a new snapshot.

### Usage

Probe the server clock for advisory SSE transport timing estimates.

### Inputs

No parameters.

### Invariants

now is server Unix epoch milliseconds at response generation, not a synchronized clock or a guaranteed network latency measurement. The response is no-store.

### Effects

Reads the current process clock only.

### Recovery

Repeat the probe to update an estimate; network delay and clock changes can affect it.

post.description:
### Usage

Append advisory client transport samples for diagnostics.

### Inputs

JSON body up to 256 KiB with samples array of at most 1000 entries. Each retained sample must be an object with a metric string of at most 32 characters and serialized size at most 4096 bytes.

### Invariants

Invalid individual samples are skipped; written counts only retained entries. Server timestamp and truncated user agent replace any same-named sample fields.

### Effects

Appends JSONL under the agent directory, rotating the existing file after it exceeds 20 MiB.

### Recovery

A retry after an uncertain response can append duplicates; these metrics are advisory, not a deduplicated delivery log.

### Usage

Open or resume an owner-bound staged upload.

### Inputs

Send id, host, name, size in bytes and type.

### Invariants

The upload id is bound to its owner and host; matching generation metadata matters when resuming.

### Effects

Creates or resumes staged host data and returns received bytes and possibly a completion proof.

### Recovery

Use the returned offset to resume; do not assume a lost response means nothing was staged.

type.description: Declared media type of the upload.

proof.description: Completion proof when the upload was already complete.

### Usage

Abort a staged upload.

### Inputs

Use the upload id and optional registered owning host id when this web server no longer has the upload's in-memory registration.

### Invariants

The request is scoped to the upload owner.

### Effects

Deletes staged data immediately or queues cleanup for the host’s next hello.

### Recovery

A 204 does not imply an offline host has already deleted its staged file.

put.description:
### Usage

Append the next binary chunk to a staged upload.

### Inputs

The id identifies an upload owned by the current web session; offset is a nonnegative safe-integer byte count and the raw body is at most 1 MiB.

### Invariants

The offset must equal the host’s received byte count; a mismatch returns 409 with received.

### Effects

Advances staged data and returns done and, on completion, a proof for later claiming.

### Recovery

On offset conflict resume from received. After an uncertain response replay upload start with the same id, name, type and size to obtain the host's acknowledged offset before resending bytes.

### Additional protocol details

Chunks are owner-bound and acknowledged after the host persists them. A 409 upload_offset response includes the authoritative received offset.

schema.description: Host-confirmed staged upload progress after a binary chunk.

done.description: Whether the declared upload size has been received.

proof.description: Completion proof for claiming this upload generation in a later outbox command; it does not authorize upload writes or cancellation.

received.description: Total staged bytes accepted by the host, and the next required offset.

get.description:
### Usage

Obtain a usage report derived from local session transcripts and the persistent usage database, not an authoritative provider bill.

### Inputs

range accepts today, 7d, 30d, 90d, month or all (default 30d); granularity accepts daily, monthly or projects (default daily). Optional project filters the report. from and to are integer Unix epoch milliseconds and override range only when both parse as numbers; refresh=true or 1 invalidates caches. Invalid range or granularity falls back to its default.

### Invariants

Parsed usage and file listings are cached; pricing is calculated from available usage and model rates and can be incomplete or estimated.

### Effects

A refresh invalidates in-memory usage and session-file-list caches; report generation can synchronize the local SQLite database.

### Recovery

Retry a failed read; use refresh when underlying files changed but cached data appears stale. Estimates should not be used to reconcile invoices without provider records.

post.description:
### Usage

Exchange the configured web password for a browser session cookie; password protection is optional and this route returns 404 when disabled.

### Inputs

Send JSON containing a string password in a body no larger than 8 KiB. Invalid credentials return 401.

### Invariants

The cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, path / and has a configured maximum age. Secure is selected from the request protocol, including the first X-Forwarded-Proto value, so the proxy supplying that header must be trusted.

### Effects

A valid password creates a session and sets its cookie; it does not configure the password.

### Recovery

Retry with the correct password after a 401; after an uncertain response, check whether the browser received a usable cookie before issuing another session.

### Additional protocol details

On success sets an HttpOnly session cookie.

put.description:
### Usage

Patch persisted server settings; browser-local preferences are separate.

### Inputs

Optional fields include agentEnv as KEY=VALUE text or an object and uploadRetentionDays as 1–3650 days or null.

### Invariants

Omitted fields are preserved; supplied agentEnv replaces its map and invalid or reserved names are rejected.

### Effects

Saves settings, may sync running sessions, broadcasts changed browser transport and pushes retention to hosts.

### Recovery

Read server settings after an uncertain response before retrying the patch.

### Additional protocol details

Agent environment variable names are validated against the reserved-name policy.

get.description:
### Usage

List worktrees or inspect branches, creation settings or creation status.

### Inputs

action selects branches, settings or status; otherwise cwd lists worktrees. hostId selects the daemon.

### Invariants

projectPath and cwd are host-machine paths; status uses the job id.

### Effects

Branch discovery refreshes remote-tracking refs and queries GitHub if configured. No worktree is created.

### Recovery

Poll status or refresh the listing as creation progresses.

post.description:
### Usage

Prepare, create, configure or delete a registered workspace.

### Inputs

Send action, action-specific input and optional hostId; prepare requires projectPath, nonblank prompt and the selected baseRef.

### Invariants

Prepare requires a registered Git project; if naming fails or exceeds 10 seconds it uses a generic name and random branch. Cancellation before creation prevents it from starting.

### Effects

Prepare and create start creation; settings can change configuration; delete removes a registered worktree and invalidates session lists.

### Recovery

After an uncertain result inspect job status and worktree state before retrying; deletion is not assumed rolled back.
